translation_en: Sulayman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us. They said: ‘Isa ibn Yunus informed us: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Urwah, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said: Eleven women sat together and pledged among themselves that they would conceal nothing about their husbands’ affairs. The first said, ‘My husband is like camel meat left on the top of a mountain: it is neither easy to climb up to nor fat enough to be worth carrying away.’ The second said, ‘I will not spread my husband’s story. I fear I could not leave him; if I describe him, I will mention all his twists and bumps.’ The third said, ‘My husband is tall and awkward. If I speak, I will be divorced; if I keep silent, I will be left hanging.’ The fourth said, ‘My husband is like a night in Tihamah: neither hot nor cold, with no fear and no weariness.’ The fifth said, ‘When my husband enters, he is like a leopard; when he goes out, he is like a lion, and he does not ask about what he has left behind.’ The sixth said, ‘When my husband eats, he gobbles; when he drinks, he drains the vessel; when he lies down, he wraps himself up, and he does not put his hand in to learn what is troubling me.’ The seventh said, ‘My husband is gloomy—or dull—thickheaded; every ailment is his. He wounds you, breaks your bones, or does both to you.’ The eighth said, ‘My husband’s touch is like a rabbit’s, and his scent is like zarneb.’ The ninth said, ‘My husband has lofty pillars, a long sword strap, great heaps of ashes, and a house close to the gathering place.’ The tenth said, ‘My husband is Malik, and what is Malik? Malik is better than that. He has many camels that kneel to rest and are taken out to pasture only a little. When they hear the sound of the lute, they know they are doomed.’ The eleventh said, ‘My husband is Abu Zar‘. And what is Abu Zar‘? He adorned my ears with jewelry and filled my upper arms with fat. He made me so proud of myself that I became pleased with myself. He found me among a poor family with a few sheep, then placed me among people with neighing horses, grunting camels, grain being threshed, and grain being cleaned. With him, I speak without being criticized; I sleep until late in the morning; and I drink my fill.’ As for Abu Zar‘’s mother, what was Abu Zar‘’s mother like? Her storage bags were full, and her house was spacious. Abu Zar‘’s son—what was Abu Zar‘’s son like? His bed was as narrow as the unsheathed blade of a sword, and an arm of a young goat was enough to satisfy him. Abu Zar‘’s daughter—what was Abu Zar‘’s daughter like? She obeyed her father and her mother, filled her garment, and made her co-wife envious. Abu Zar‘’s servant girl—what was Abu Zar‘’s servant girl like? She did not spread our talk carelessly, did not waste our provisions, and did not fill our house with rubbish.’ She said: Abu Zar‘ went out while the milk vessels were being churned. He met a woman who had two sons like leopards playing beneath her waist with two pomegranates. He divorced me and married her. After him, I married a noble man who rode a fine horse, carried a spear from Khatt, and brought me abundant livestock. He gave me a pair of every kind of animal that returns in the evening and said, ‘Eat, Mother of Zar‘, and provide for your family.’ She said: If I gathered everything he gave me, it would not amount to the smallest vessel of Abu Zar‘. ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘I am to you as Abu Zar‘ was to Umm Zar‘.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Sa‘id ibn Salamah narrated from Hisham the wording, ‘and she does not make our house a nest.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Some narrated ‘fa ataqammahu’ with the letter mim, and this is more correct.
